Speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
Effective line: The great pantry door swings open. Somewhere beyond, something smells incredible.
Suggested line: The great pantry door swings open. Somewhere beyond, something smells incredible. Underneath it, faintly, something smells of hot iron.
Why: Plants the arms-factory secret on the very first step in, without a word of exposition.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Your HP is full, and the chef says there are no seconds. You both know this is a serving of fiction.
Suggested line: Your HP is already full. A chef refills your plate anyway. Here, being full is treated as a misunderstanding.
Why: The current joke is muddled; this one comes straight from the zone's 'nobody leaves hungry' culture.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: A hidden stash! Nobody tasted that one. Lettuce rejoice.
Suggested line: A hidden stash! Unsampled, unsauced and all yours.
Why: The Pantry Run summary already spends the lettuce pun; this nods to the Special Sauce instead.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The golem steps aside. The way is open.
Suggested line: The golem steps aside with the slow dignity of a roast being carved. The way is open.
Why: A flat system line gets one image of the knightly meat golems.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You ladle some soup. Delicious, but you are already stuffed to the brim.
Suggested line: You ladle some soup, look at it, and pour it back. You are full. The fountain takes it well.
Why: Replaces a plain statement with a small, deadpan beat.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You fell in the gravy! Somebody fishes you out and sets you on dry ground. (-1 HP)
Suggested line: You fall in the gravy. A passing chef fishes you out with a ladle and checks you for seasoning. (-1 HP)
Why: Present tense like the rest of the narration, and a chef-shaped joke instead of 'Somebody'.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: - Guard the kingdom (with golems)
Suggested line: - Guard the kingdom (with golems. Defensive golems. Please stop saying the other word.)
Why: The brief's 'chefs flinch at the word weapon' finally appears on the zone's first sign.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Welcome to the far side. The gates ahead are guarded by golems, as is the custom.
Suggested line: Welcome to the far side. The gates ahead are guarded by golems, as is the custom. One wants saffron, one wants a favour, one wants a fight.
Why: Tells the player the three gate conditions at a glance, in sign rhythm.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Please do not bite the buildings. They are load-bearing cake.
Suggested line: Please do not bite the buildings. The mayor's house is down to two layers, and he knows it was a visitor.
Why: 'Load-bearing' is Bertram's owned gag; this keeps the joke local to cake town.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Four ingredients, in the right order, tastes like victory.
Suggested line: Four ingredients, in the right order. Anything else tastes like a lesson.
Why: The current sentence does not parse; this reads cleanly and keeps the hint.

Speaker: Basil
Effective line: Psst. Hello. I'm Basil, line cook. Ladle in one hand, nerves in the other. We Gourmands feed the kingdom and protect it. Every plate is a promise. Every golem is a guard.
Suggested line: Psst. Basil, line cook. Ladle in one hand, nerves in the other. We Gourmands feed the kingdom and protect it: chefs cook, golems guard. Lately the golems have been... practising.
Why: Swaps two poster slogans for a nervous hint of the war programme; Basil's voice, same fact.

Speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
Effective line: Don't tell the Grand Chef I said anything. She hears everything. She just never tastes anything.
Suggested line: Don't tell the Grand Chef I said anything. Last cook who complained got promoted to taste tester. We haven't seen him since.
Why: Basil already does 'hears everything, never tastes'; this gives Tarragon his own fear and pays off the taste-tester signs.

Speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
Effective line: I'm hungry and a bit scared. If either came with a side dish, we'd be sorted.
Suggested line: I'm so hungry I looked at a Refusemancer compost heap and thought 'starter'. Don't tell anyone. I'd never live it down.
Why: Uses the Gourmand vs 'garbage eaters' rivalry from someone sincerely inside the culture.

Speaker: Madame Mirepoix
Effective line: Gourmand-issue, inspected by the Test Kitchen as of this year. The stamp is on the decorative cake, which has never looked more unappetizing.
Suggested line: Gourmand-issue, inspected by the Test Kitchen as of this year. They stamped my decorative cake. Right on the rosette. I have not forgiven them.
Why: The current line is hard to follow; this keeps the stamp and sets up the cake with snoot.

Speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
Effective line: The pantry's stocked until tomorrow, when we do it all again. Fetching has a wonderful sense of repetition; I'd like to send it back.
Suggested line: The pantry's stocked until tomorrow, when we do it all again. I'm not complaining. I'm fetching. They look similar from a distance.
Why: The 'send it back' turn is muddled; this is cleaner overworked-intern panic.

Speaker: Madame Mirepoix
Effective line: One Hearty Pot Pie, darling. Honey, basil and a ghost pepper into the Grand Oven by the arch. I shall wait. I have cake.
Suggested line: One Hearty Pot Pie, darling. Honey, basil and a ghost pepper into the Grand Oven by the arch. I shall wait. I have a cake to look at.
Why: Her cake is decorative; the tweak lands her running gag and its later payoff.

Speaker: Professor Pate
Effective line: Back to improve your score? Splendid. Knowledge, like a good roux, wants patience. And butter. Mostly butter.
Suggested line: Back for more? Splendid. A footnote, while it simmers: the Capital's school lunches were excellent once. Hot, free, balanced. Then came the paste.
Why: Repeats his bark almost word for word; this works in Primm's genuinely good reform and Crumb's paste.

Speaker: (gate golem)
Effective line: The golem stands firm.
Suggested line: The golem stands firm, like an aspic that has made up its mind.
Why: One food image for a bare system line.

Speaker: Colonel Casserole
Effective line: En garde, traveller. A duel of honour. Lids up. Yes, Chef.
Suggested line: En garde! Thirty years of service, and I have never once boiled over. Until now. Yes, Chef.
Why: The event line nearly repeats his intro; this gives the half-health turn its own beat.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You find rations, ladles and ladle-shaped weapons. Take what you can carry; someone has overthought serving suggestions.
Suggested line: You find rations, ladles and ladle-shaped weapons in crates marked SERVING UTENSILS (DEFENSIVE). Take what you can carry.
Why: The euphemism is the zone's joke engine; the golems own 'overthought' ladles.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Great vats of the Special Sauce bubble in the dark. This is where the corruption is made.
Suggested line: Great vats of the Special Sauce bubble in the dark. A clipboard on the rail reads: BATCH 3,652. TASTED BY: (blank).
Why: Shows the corruption instead of telling it: ten years of daily batches, nobody tasting.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Blueprints, recipe cards and signed memos fill the cabinets. Every handwritten note signed by the Grand Chef leans the wrong way, as if written by someone who has only ever read about left-handedness.
Suggested line: Blueprints, recipe cards and signed memos fill the cabinets. Every note signed by the Grand Chef is in perfect copperplate, without one gravy stain. Real chefs' notes are mostly gravy stain.
Why: Turns the clunky left-handed clue into the zone's theme: appearance over substance.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: - Guard the kingdom (with golems)
Suggested line: - Guard the kingdom (with golems; the cannons are ovens now)
Why: The freed sign shows the zone has changed instead of repeating the old line.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: To {town}, through the great pantry door. Wipe your feet - we just mopped, but your sample is yours now; take two.
Suggested line: To {town}, through the great pantry door. Wipe your feet; we just mopped. Free samples by the door. Take two. Nobody is checking.
Why: The current line is tangled; this shows the freedom in plain sign rhythm.

Speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
Effective line: Tarragon! Sous-Chef! Free!
Suggested line: Tarragon! Sous-Chef! Fetcher of things! I caught up with lunch!
Why: Pays off his running gag of never catching up with lunch.

Speaker: (narration/UI)
Effective line: Official likeness withdrawn. It never captured the person who fed us.
Suggested line: Official likeness withdrawn. It never captured the person who fed us. (Also: whose chin is that?)
Why: Restores the 'Whose chin is that?' half of the chin gag pair the voice bible flags for restore.
